column1: health|The condition of a person's body and mind.|The centre offers advice on improving health at work.
wellbeing|A general state of being healthy and comfortable.|Regular breaks can support employee wellbeing.
clinic|A place providing medical advice or treatment.|The clinic accepts new patients from this area.
surgery|A doctor's workplace for consultations and treatment.|Call the surgery to arrange an appointment.
hospital|A place providing treatment for illness or injury.|The bus stops outside the main hospital entrance.
pharmacy|A place where medicines are prepared and sold.|The pharmacy is open late on weekdays.
chemist|A shop selling medicines and health products.|Ask the chemist about the dosage instructions.
GP|A doctor who treats common health problems in the community.|You should register with a local GP after moving.
doctor|A qualified professional who diagnoses and treats illness.|The doctor asked when the symptoms began.
nurse|A trained professional who cares for patients.|The nurse will explain how to care for the wound.
dentist|A professional who treats teeth and gums.|Book a check-up with the dentist before your trip.
optician|A professional who checks vision or supplies glasses.|The optician can adjust your new glasses.
patient|Someone receiving medical care.|Each patient should complete the registration form.
medical record|A written history of someone's health and treatment.|Please ask your previous clinic to transfer your medical record.
medical history|Information about previous illnesses and treatments.|The nurse will ask about your medical history.
symptom|A change in the body that may indicate illness.|Tell the doctor about any new symptom.
illness|A condition that affects someone's health.|Notify your supervisor if illness prevents you from working.
infection|An illness caused by harmful organisms entering the body.|Wash the cut carefully to reduce the risk of infection.
injury|Physical harm to the body.|Report any workplace injury to the first-aid officer.
pain|An unpleasant physical feeling caused by illness or injury.|Explain where the pain occurs and how long it lasts.
ache|A continuous, usually dull pain.|I have an ache in my back after lifting boxes.
fever|An unusually high body temperature.|The receptionist asked whether the child had a fever.
cough|A sudden action pushing air from the throat.|Tell the pharmacist how long you have had the cough.
cold|A common illness affecting the nose and throat.|She stayed home because she had a bad cold.
flu|An infectious illness often causing fever and aching muscles.|The clinic offers flu vaccinations before winter.
allergy|A harmful reaction to a normally harmless substance.|Please mention any food allergy when booking the meal.
asthma|A condition that can make breathing difficult.|The trip organiser needs to know about your asthma.
rash|An area of irritated or marked skin.|Seek advice if the rash spreads or becomes painful.
swelling|An increase in the size of a body part after injury or illness.|The nurse checked the swelling around my ankle.
bruise|A coloured mark caused by damage under the skin.|A large bruise appeared after I slipped on the stairs.
cut|An injury where the skin has been broken.|Clean the cut before applying a dressing.
burn|An injury caused by heat or another damaging substance.|The first-aid guide explains what to do for a minor burn.
sprain|An injury caused by stretching tissue around a joint.|The doctor said the ankle sprain needed rest.
fracture|A break in a bone.|The hospital confirmed a small fracture in her wrist.
treatment|Care intended to improve an illness or injury.|The clinic will discuss your treatment options.
therapy|A planned treatment for a physical or mental condition.|The referral includes several sessions of physical therapy.
recovery|The process of returning to health after illness or injury.|Allow enough time for recovery before returning to heavy work.
specialist|A professional with expert knowledge in a particular area.|The GP referred her to a skin specialist.
prescription|A doctor's written instruction for supplying medicine.|Take the prescription to your usual pharmacy.
medicine|A substance used to treat or prevent illness.|Keep the medicine out of children's reach.
medication|Medicine used for a particular condition.|Tell the nurse about any medication you take.
dose|The amount of medicine taken at one time.|Do not take more than the recommended dose.
tablet|A small solid piece of medicine.|Take one tablet with water as directed.
capsule|Medicine enclosed in a small dissolvable shell.|Do not open the capsule unless the pharmacist advises it.
ointment|A thick substance applied to the skin for treatment.|Apply the ointment according to the instructions.
dressing|A covering used to protect a wound.|The nurse showed me how to change the dressing.
bandage|Material wrapped around an injury for protection or support.|The first-aid kit contains a clean bandage.
vaccination|Treatment that helps protect against a particular infection.|Bring your vaccination record to the travel clinic.
check-up|A routine examination to assess health.|I have booked a dental check-up for next week.
blood pressure|The pressure of blood within the blood vessels.|The nurse will measure your blood pressure.
blood test|An examination of a sample of blood.|The clinic will contact you about your blood test result.
X-ray|An image used to examine bones or other internal structures.|The doctor requested an X-ray after the fall.
scan|A medical image used to examine part of the body.|Your appointment letter explains how to prepare for the scan.
emergency|A serious situation requiring immediate action.|Use this number only in an emergency.
ambulance|A vehicle carrying people who need urgent medical care.|An ambulance arrived at the accident scene.
first aid|Immediate basic care given after illness or injury.|The workplace provides first aid training for volunteers.
first-aid kit|A collection of basic supplies for treating minor injuries.|The first-aid kit is kept beside reception.
urgent|Needing attention without delay.|Tell reception if you need an urgent appointment.
appointment reminder|A message reminding someone of a scheduled visit.|The clinic sends an appointment reminder by text.
waiting room|A room where people wait for a service.|Please remain in the waiting room until your name is called.
carer|Someone who regularly helps a person needing support.|A carer may accompany the patient to the appointment.
disability|A condition that may affect everyday activities or access.|Tell the organiser about any disability-related access needs.
wheelchair|A chair with wheels used by someone who has difficulty walking.|There is space for a wheelchair on the shuttle.
crutch|A support used to help someone walk after injury.|The physiotherapist checked the height of each crutch.
hearing aid|A device that helps someone hear sounds.|The receptionist asked whether a hearing aid was being used.
eye test|An examination of how well someone can see.|You can book an eye test online.
diet|The food and drink someone usually consumes.|The adviser suggested a more varied diet.
balanced diet|Eating a suitable variety and amount of foods.|The community class explains how to plan a balanced diet.
exercise routine|A regular plan of physical activity.|Choose an exercise routine that fits your work schedule.
fitness|The ability to do physical activity comfortably.|The beginners' class helps improve general fitness.
sleep|The period of rest when a person is not awake.|Shift workers may need advice about maintaining regular sleep.
rest|Time spent relaxing rather than working or exercising.|The doctor recommended rest after the minor injury.
stress|Mental or physical pressure caused by difficult demands.|The staff service offers help with work-related stress.
anxiety|A feeling of worry or unease.|Speak to the counsellor if anxiety is affecting your study.
mental health|The condition of someone's emotional and psychological wellbeing.|The college provides confidential mental health support.
support group|People who meet to share experiences and help each other.|The support group meets at the centre every Tuesday.
hygiene|Practices that help keep people and places clean and healthy.|Food handlers must follow strict hygiene procedures.
handwashing|Cleaning hands with water and soap.|The poster explains the correct handwashing procedure.
smoke-free|Not allowing smoking.|All indoor areas of the building are smoke-free.
wellness programme|Organised activities that support health and wellbeing.|The company wellness programme includes lunchtime walks.
physiotherapist|A professional who helps restore movement after injury.|The physiotherapist suggested exercises for my shoulder.
diagnosis|The identification of an illness or injury.|The doctor explained the diagnosis in plain language.
referral|An arrangement directing someone to another professional.|You need a referral to see this specialist.
dosage|Instructions about how much medicine to take and when.|Check the dosage on the label carefully.
side effect|An unwanted effect of a medicine or treatment.|Ask the pharmacist about any possible side effect.
repeat prescription|An authorisation to receive ongoing medication again.|Request your repeat prescription before your medicine runs out.
over-the-counter|Available from a shop without a doctor's prescription.|Ask whether an over-the-counter treatment is suitable.
immunisation|The process of developing protection against an infection.|The clinic sends reminders about childhood immunisation.
screening|A check intended to identify a condition before symptoms appear.|The invitation explains where to attend the screening.
consent|Permission given after understanding what is proposed.|The nurse will ask for consent before the procedure.
confidentiality|The duty to keep personal information private.|The clinic explained its rules on patient confidentiality.
mobility|The ability to move around.|The centre provides support for people with reduced mobility.
nutrition|The relationship between food and health.|The workshop provides practical advice on nutrition.
hydration|Having enough water in the body.|The outdoor-work briefing includes advice on hydration.
counselling|Professional support through discussion of personal difficulties.|Free counselling is available to registered students.
sanitation|Systems and practices for safely managing waste and cleanliness.|The campsite has improved its sanitation facilities.
disinfect|To clean something to reduce harmful organisms.|Staff disinfect shared equipment after each session.
sterile|Free from living organisms that could cause infection.|The nurse used a sterile dressing.
prevention|Action taken to stop a problem from occurring.|The workshop focuses on the prevention of workplace injuries.
rehabilitation|Support that helps someone recover abilities after illness or injury.|The rehabilitation programme helps her return to work safely.
